title: One spritesheet with background-position vs 16 separate image files
variable: single atlas texture vs one texture per sprite
claim: Antipattern #47 from web-performance-antipatterns-50.md: 'many separate small images instead of a spritesheet/atlas - per-image state and upload overhead.' Gameface makes this more pointed than the web does: RAG 15-tooling.md 'Tracking Texture Thrashing with Memory Counters' names sprite frames loaded as separate images as a leading cause of texture thrashing, and the engine's Instaload path is built around external files. Atlasing is real work for an art pipeline, so the ratio decides whether it earns its place.
result: CONFIRMED, but only at scale and only modestly: no reliable difference at 30 or 100 tiles, then Paint 1.69x at 300 with GPU inside the guardrail at 1.11x. Sixteen separate textures cost measurably more to draw than one atlas once there are 300 draws pulling from them, and nothing at all below that. Atlasing is therefore worth the art-pipeline effort for dense repeated content - inventory grids, icon walls, minimap markers - and is not worth it for a HUD with a few dozen sprites. IMPORTANT LIMIT: this measures steady-state drawing only. The 16-file variant also occupies more texture memory and more Instaload entries, and RAG 15-tooling.md names exactly this shape as a cause of texture thrashing - none of which this row can see. A modest per-frame ratio is not a clean bill of health for shipping loose sprites.
notes: Applicability gate: DIRECT. url() and background-position are both supported and were verified against the Player. Rule 1: one variable, how many textures the same artwork is delivered in. Rule 2: identical DOM, identical geometry, and PIXEL-IDENTICAL output - the atlas and the 16 loose files are generated by tools/make-baked-images.js from the same spriteAt() function, so A and B render the same 16 designs in the same slots. Rule 3: identical JS apart from the single USE_SHEET constant; both pages define both paths and both set backgroundImage inline, so the inline-style machinery is exercised equally. Rule 4 EXCEPTION: the two variants load different assets - that IS the variable. The 16 sprites are deliberately distinct from one another (verified: 16 unique file hashes) so the engine cannot dedupe them into a single texture and quietly erase the difference being measured. Rule 5: 300 tiles occupy 1852x1032 inside 1920x1080. Rule 6: static page plus the shared root-nudge damage driver. Rule 7: sprite choice derives from the loop index. Rule 8: counts 30/100/300 tiles drawn, against a fixed 16 distinct sprites. Rule 9: plain HTML/CSS/JS. Rule 10: expected axis is GPU - if the engine binds a texture per draw, B should cost more there while Paint and Styles stay flat. LIMIT: this measures steady-state drawing, not load time or memory. The 16-file variant also occupies more texture memory and more Instaload entries, neither of which this row can see.
